2609.16991.title: Autoformalizing Argumentative Material Inferences
2609.16991.paper_summary: Natural language arguments are compelling before they are formally explicit. A premise supports a claim through defeasible warrants, background commitments, and exception conditions that the text leaves implicit. However, formal verification requires the opposite. Making such arguments machine-checkable requires constructing the missing commitments, not only translating given sentences into logic. Construction, however, carries a risk that translation does not: a system free to add premises can make any claim provable, and a formally valid proof may assert the claim outright, prove it without the original premise, or establish more than the claim itself. We address this problem by formulating autoformalization for argumentative material inference as guard completion, in which non-monotonic material support is turned into monotonic formal inference relative to an explicitly constructed guard set. A completion is accepted only when its proof both passes the theorem prover and survives contrastive tests of premise dependence and claim selectivity. We implement this formulation in GUARD, a neuro-symbolic framework in which LLMs construct and formalize candidate guards, Isabelle/HOL verifies the resulting theories and returns step-level feedback for iterative refinement, and the system abstains when no faithful completion can be reached. Our empirical results on Debatepedia and ARCT using different LLMs demonstrate that GUARD yields significant improvements in verified-faithful (+35.3, +32.9 points) and substantial reductions in leakage (-25.9, -21.9 points) over the state-of-the-art LLM-driven theorem proving approach. Moreover, we show that the symbolic soft critique and the explicit assumption layer account for most of these gains, with the soft critique also improving the initial validity of the elicited context and reducing the number of iterations required for successful verification.
2609.16991.paper_summary_zh: 自然語言的論證在正式明確之前是引人注目的。前提通過可推翻的保證、背景承諾和文本隱含的例外條件來支持一個主張。然而，正式驗證需要相反的方式。使這些論證可以機器檢查需要構建缺失的承諾，而不僅僅是將給定的句子翻譯成邏輯。然而，構建帶來的風險是翻譯所不具備的：一個可以自由添加前提的系統可以使任何主張可證明，並且一個形式上有效的證明可能會直接聲明該主張，無需原始前提即可證明它，或建立超過主張本身的內容。我們通過將論證材料推理的自動形式化表述為保護完成來解決這個問題，其中非單調的材料支持轉變為相對於明確構建的保護集的單調形式推理。只有當其證明同時通過定理證明器並且經受住前提依賴性和主張選擇性的對比測試時，才接受一個完成。我們在GUARD中實現了這一表述，這是一個神經符號框架，其中LLMs構建和形式化候選保護，Isabelle/HOL驗證所產生的理論並返回逐步反饋以進行迭代改進，當無法達到忠實的完成時系統會放棄。我們在Debatepedia和ARCT上使用不同的LLMs的實證結果表明，GUARD在經過驗證的忠實性上（+35.3，+32.9分）顯著改善，並在泄漏方面（-25.9，-21.9分）大幅減少，超過了最先進的LLM驅動定理證明方法。此外，我們顯示符號軟批評和明確假設層解釋了這些增益的大部分，軟批評還改善了引出上下文的初始有效性，並減少了成功驗證所需的迭代次數。
